raw: #1: = ♦ It is mentioned, in the 15th book of Polybius, that the Carthaginian ambassadors, in token of humiliation and entreaty, prostrated themselves on the ground and kissed the feet of the members of the council. In Xenophon (Cyrop., lib. vii.) it is stated that certain persons kissed the feet of Cyrus, and wept for joy. In the 9th book of Polybius, it is said that when Hannibal approached Rome, the Roman ladies went to the temples and supplicated the gods, "washing the pavement of the temples with their hair," as their custom was on such occasions: πλυνουσαι ταις κομαις τα των ἱερων ἐδαφη· τουτο γαρ ἐθος ἐστι—. Sternitur et pedibus crebro pavida oscula figens.—Sil. Ital., lib. xi.
